'''''Phlegmariurus dentatus''''' is a species of plant in the family [[Lycopodiaceae]] that is [[endemic]] to the [[Portugal|Portuguese]] [[archipelago]]s of the [[Azores]] and [[Madeira]]. 

==Distribution and habitat==
''P. dentatus'' is widespread in the Azores and may be found on the islands of [[São Miguel Island|São Miguel]], [[Terceira]], [[São Jorge Island|São Jorge]], [[Pico Island|Pico]], [[Faial Island|Faial]], [[Flores Island (Azores)|Flores]] and [[Corvo Island|Corvo]]. It is less common in Madeira, occurring only on [[Madeira Island]]. It can be found growing on damp and sheltered slopes, in [[Gully|gullies]], on [[Bank (geography)|banks]] above [[Levada (Madeira)|levadas]], and at the edges of roads and forests at elevations of {{cvt|200-2300|m}} [[above sea level]].<ref name=iucn/>

==Description==
''P. dentatus'' is a stout, upright [[lycophyte]] growing to {{cvt|41|cm}} tall. The leaves are [[Glossary of leaf morphology#Linear|linear]]-[[Glossary of leaf morphology#Lanceolate|lanceolate]] in shape, measuring approximately {{cvt|9|mm}} by {{cvt|1.2|mm}}, with [[Glossary of leaf morphology#dentate|toothed margins]]. [[Stomata]] are present only on the underside of leaves. It branches [[Glossary of botanical terms#dichotomous|dichotomously]] and lacks [[Gemma (botany)|gemmae]].<ref name=FM>{{cite book |editor1-last=Press |editor1-first=J.
